title: EEmo-Logic: A Unified Dataset and Multi-Stage Framework for Comprehensive Image-Evoked Emotion Assessment
claim: One model trained on a comprehensive dataset beats strong baselines on multi-task QA and also gives fine-grained, reasoned assessments.
layout: 2 stacked panels: (a) QA example plus radar chart, (b) cartoon capabilities with reasoning output
description: The figure has two dashed-border panels, one above the other. Panel (a), "Emotion QA", has a green header and a flower and hummingbird photo. Beneath it is a multiple-choice question about the dominance level of the evoked emotion, with a confused cartoon person beside it. A legend lists seven models with their answers: six baselines answer B and are marked with red crosses, and EEmo-Logic (Ours) answers A and has a green check. On the right is an eight-axis radar chart covering perception, description, ranking and overall tasks. The red EEmo-Logic polygon encloses all the others. Panel (b), "Emotion Logic", has a blue header. A robot labelled EEmo-Logic, fed by the EEmoDB database icon, produces thought bubbles with valence, arousal and dominance gauges, a dominant emotion and an emotion ranking. At lower right, a dog photo and a think/answer chain-of-thought output rank the top three emotions.
caption: Trained on our constructed EEmoDB via a two-stage paradigm, EEmo-Logic (a) achieves robust question-answering performance on EEmo-Bench, and (b) demonstrates strong capabilities in fine-grained emotion assessment and causal reasoning.
abstract: Understanding the multi-dimensional attributes and intensity nuances of image-evoked emotions is pivotal for advancing machine empathy and empowering diverse human-computer interaction applications. However, existing models are still limited to coarse-grained emotion perception or deficient reasoning capabilities. To bridge this gap, we introduce EEmoDB, the largest image-evoked emotion understanding dataset to date. It features $5$ analysis dimensions spanning $5$ distinct task categories, facilitating comprehensive interpretation. Specifically, we compile $1.2M$ question-answering (QA) pairs (EEmoDB-QA) from $125K$ images via automated generation, alongside a $36K$ dataset (EEmoDB-Assess) curated from $25K$ images for fine-grained assessment. Furthermore, we propose EEmo-Logic, an all-in-one multimodal large language model (MLLM) developed via instruction fine-tuning and task-customized group relative preference optimization (GRPO) with novel reward design. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EEmo-Logic achieves robust performance in in-domain and cross-domain datasets, excelling in emotion QA and fine-grained assessment. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/workerred/EEmo-Logic.
